Church members erupted in cheers on Sunday as Pastor Jimmy Odukoya arrived for the service at The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, with the excitement generating noise that almost disrupted the ongoing praise session. His arrival came amid the leadership crisis rocking the church, following a court order restraining him from presenting himself as its Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head. Before his arrival, the social media tension and drama of the past week did not appear to extend to the church premises, as the atmosphere was relatively calm and members went about their activities as though nothing had happened. The heavy security presence around the premises was, however, one of the few indications that something might have happened. Before the service began, church members were seen discussing the unfolding developments in pairs and small groups. They appeared more careful with their conversations, seemingly conscious that journalists, bloggers and other visitors could be present. An opening prayer was led by a minister simply identified as Pastor Ezeogwu, while members settled down for the service. “The fowler’s snare has been broken,” the minister prayed, drawing a thunderous “Amen” from the congregation. In another part of the prayer, he said, “Do not allow us to join the column of gossips,” a remark that appeared to speak to the controversy surrounding the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had issued an interim order restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church. The order, made by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin on Wednesday, November 18, followed an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church. The court also restrained Odukoya, either personally or through proxies, from interfering with or disrupting the church’s activities, governance and other business. However, the certified true copy of the order did not direct the closure or sealing of the church premises. The court adjourned the matter until December 1 for mention, while the interim orders remain subject to further proceedings. The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as Senior Pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the interim spiritual and administrative leader of the church. However, Jimmy Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, insisting that his appointment in September 2023 was valid.
